articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft's April Patch Tuesday is serving 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. When your monthly security update looks like a CVE phone book, maybe it's time to question some life choices.

articles.title: PCPJack Credential Stealer Exploits 5 CVEs to Spread Worm-Like Across Cloud Systems
articles.summary: Ivanti EPMM gets pwned again with CVE-2026-6973, granting admin-level RCE to attackers who probably didn't even need to try that hard. At this point, Ivanti vulnerabilities are like clockwork—terrifying, predictable clockwork.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Edge Plaintext Passwords, ICS 0-Days, Patch-or-Die Alerts and 25+ New Stories
articles.summary: PAN-OS buffer overflow (CVE-2026-0300) is being actively exploited for root access and espionage since April 9th. Your $50k firewall just became someone else's front door—hope you kept the receipt.

articles.title: Maine Dems to Vote on Condemning DCCC Interference in House Primary
articles.summary: ShinyHunters breached Instructure's Canvas LMS, exposing the terrifying reality of how much trust schools blindly dump on their vendors. When your kid's homework portal becomes a data goldmine, someone's asking the wrong security questions.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: AI-Powered Phishing, Android Spying Tool, Linux Exploit, GitHub RCE & More
articles.summary: Instructure breach just got scarier: hacker claims 280 million records stolen from 8,809 schools and universities. That's not a breach, that's educational infrastructure annihilation with a side of identity theft for an entire generation.

articles.title: Milestone 1.0.0 Release of APK Downloader `apkeep` Powers Research on Android Apps
articles.summary: Germany finally puts a face to 'UNKN,' the ghost who ran REvil and GandCrab ransomware empires. 31-year-old Daniil Shchukin managed 130+ cyberattacks before his OPSEC failed him—respect the hustle, condemn the victims.

articles.title: Has CISA Finally Found Its New Leader in Tom Parker?
articles.summary: NSA whistleblower William Binney's 'turnkey totalitarian state' warning hits different when you realize we're already living in it. Politicians change, surveillance empires don't—time to dismantle the machine before it gets worse.

articles.title: EFF and 18 Organizations Urge UK Policymakers to Prioritize Addressing the Roots of Online Harm
articles.summary: The SECURE Data Act is privacy theater masquerading as legislation—House Republicans dropped this toothless draft without bipartisan support. When your 'privacy protection' would actually weaken existing state laws, maybe call it what it is: corporate capture.

articles.title: The network password was a key plot point in one of the most famous movies of all time
articles.summary: 60% of MD5 hashes crack in under an hour, making World Password Day feel like World Security Theater Day. If you're still using MD5 in 2026, you're not just behind the times—you're actively helping attackers.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence is mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens through compromised routers like it's 2003 all over again. Your ancient Linksys just became Moscow's favorite authentication buffet—firmware updates aren't suggestions, people.
